title: Annotator Economics and Probe Retention Policy
author: Priya Desai
content:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference's policy for annotation economics (how we compensate human annotators and run quality control) and the lifecycle and retention policy for probe artifacts used across evals, model onboarding, and regression triage. The goal is to make probe stewardship predictable, cost-aware, privacy-compliant, and operationally auditable.

Scope:
- Applies to all probe artifacts generated or ingested by Applied ML and Evals teams, including synthetic probes, user-derived probes (anonymized), adversarial test cases, and annotator labels stored in central probe repositories.
- Includes guidance for annotator pay bands, QA pass thresholds, annotation latency targets, storage tiers, deletion/archival procedures, and exception handling.
- Excludes ephemeral debug probes created only in local development that are not pushed to shared repositories.

Definitions:
- Probe: an input (prompt, conversation, multimodal input) together with metadata and (optionally) reference labels used for evaluation.
- Annotator: a human contributor who provides labels, ratings, or quality judgments for probes. Includes internal annotators and vetted external vendors.
- Probe Artifact: files and records (JSON/YAML/CSV and attachments) stored in the probe catalog.
- Hot Storage: fast-access storage used by eval harnesses and live shadowing.
- Cold Storage: lower-cost blob storage (S3 Glacier/nearline) for archival.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Applied ML (Probe Stewards): maintain probe taxonomy, label schema, and retention metadata fields. Primary owner of this policy.
- Data Platform: implements storage lifecycle rules, access controls, and cost reports.
- Vendor Management: negotiates vendor rates, SLAs, and compliance attestations.
- Security & Privacy: approves retention periods for customer-derived probes and redaction procedures.

Annotator economics (recommended bands and pay model):
- Payment model: per-labeled-item with QA-tier multiplier. Final payout = base_rate * (1 + qa_bonus) where qa_bonus depends on audit pass rate.
- Base rate bands (USD per judgment, approximate ranges):
  * Simple binary label: $0.06 - $0.12
  * Multi-class single-turn: $0.20 - $0.45
  * Multi-turn dialog (per-turn): $0.40 - $1.10
  * Complex reasoning / chain-of-thought annotation: $1.50 - $4.00
- QA multiplier: 
  * Audit pass >= 98%: +12% bonus
  * 95% <= pass < 98%: +6% bonus
  * 90% <= pass < 95%: +0% bonus
  * pass < 90%: action: retraining and partial rework; pay withheld until rework passes.
- Minimum effective hourly guarantee for internal annotators: $18/hr equivalent (useful for long tasks with many micro judgments).
- Vendor SLA expectations: average label latency < 48 hours for standard tasks, < 24 hours for high-priority probes. Penalties apply for repeated misses.

Quality control and instrumentation:
1) Sentinel audits: 5–10% of items randomly selected for gold checks per batch.
2) Inter-annotator agreement (IAA): report Cohen's Kappa or Krippendorff alpha per task; threshold: Kappa >= 0.65 for promotion to production probes.
3) Review pipeline: failed sentinels trigger reviewer queue; repeated failures escalate to vendor management.
4) Annotator feedback loop: weekly calibration sessions and example-led remediation.

Probe metadata and minimum schema (fields required in probe catalog):
- probe_id (string), created_by (string), created_at (YYYY-MM-DD), source (synthetic | shadow | customer), sensitivity_level (public | internal | restricted), retention_tier (hot | cold | delete_on_criteria), labels (list), annotator_id (string|vendor-id), qa_pass (true|false), qa_notes (string), last_accessed (YYYY-MM-DD), linked_eval_id (string), embargo_until (YYYY-MM-DD|null).

Retention policy (default tiers and TTLs):
- Hot (default for newly created probes): 180 days from created_at unless promoted. Accessible to eval harness and shadowing pipelines.
- Cold: 3 years from created_at. Moved to cold after 180 days of inactivity or explicit archival. Retrieval windows: 24–72 hours.
- Delete-on-criteria: immediate deletion after fulfillment of legal/contractual erasure requests or on-demand for restricted customer data after NDA review.
- Permanent archive: select seed sets (curated benchmarks) may be retained indefinitely; these must have explicit product owner approval and an associated retention waiver.

Data access and privacy controls:
- All customer-derived probes default to sensitivity_level=restricted unless redacted and approved by Privacy.
- Annotator access: annotators should not see raw PII. Use programmatic redaction and privacy-preserving interfaces.
- Access logs: every read/write/restore from cold storage must be logged with user, action, and timestamp. Audit log retention: 2 years.

Cost estimation and example table (monthly cost model):
| Component | Unit | Qty | Unit Cost (USD) | Monthly Cost (USD) | Notes |
| Hot object storage | GB | 2,500 | 0.024 | 60 | S3 standard-like tier used by evals |
| Cold archival | GB | 12,000 | 0.004 | 48 | Glacier-like pricing |
| Retrieval API / egress | ops | 4,000 | 0.002 | 8 | peek/replays by evaluation harness |
| Annotation vendor spend | judgments | 200,000 | 0.30 | 60,000 | mix of task types; example only |
| QA review labor | hours | 200 | 45 | 9,000 | internal reviewers and calibration |
| Total (example) | | | | 69,116 | Budget planning input |

Operational runbook: enforcement and typical procedures
1) Daily job: retention-enforcer runs at 02:00 UTC. Steps:
   a) Query probe_catalog for items where retention_tier=hot AND created_at < now() - 180d AND last_accessed < now() - 90d.
   b) For candidates, create a move-to-cold task and notify probe steward slack channel (#probe-stewards).
   c) When moving to cold, update retention_tier and set last_moved_to_cold timestamp.
2) Weekly audit: run a probe-ttl-audit report listing items scheduled for deletion within 30 days. Notify owners.
3) Deletion procedure (manual gating for restricted):
   1. Verify legal/customer erasure token.
   2. Run redact-and-delete CLI (example below).
   3. Append deletion event to retention_audit_log.

Redact-and-delete sample CLI (reference):
$ rdc probe delete --probe-id p-12345 --redact-fields "email,ssn" --reason "customer erasure" --initiator "data-request-team"

S3 lifecycle example (JSON snippet for Data Platform):
{ "Rules": [ { "ID": "hot-to-cold", "Status": "Enabled", "Prefix": "probes/hot/", "Transition": { "Days": 180, "StorageClass": "GLACIER" } }, { "ID": "cold-expire-3y", "Status": "Enabled", "Prefix": "probes/cold/", "Expiration": { "Days": 1095 } } ] }

Metrics and dashboards (what to monitor):
- Annotation throughput (labels/day) by vendor and task type. Target: sustained throughput with <15% variance week-over-week.
- QA pass rate (gold sentinel pass %) per batch. SLO: >= 95%.
- Average time-to-label (mean and p95). Target: mean < 24h for standard tasks.
- Probe catalog storage by tier (GB) and monthly cost. Budget variance alert: >10% increase month-over-month triggers finance review.
- Retention compliance rate: % of probes older than TTL that are still in hot storage (target < 1%).

Onboarding and pay adjustment flow for new tasks:
1) Probe steward drafts task spec and rough complexity estimate.
2) Run pilot with 500 items and measure median time-per-item and QA pass rate.
3) Compute effective hourly equivalent and map to base_rate band.
4) Submit vendor rate change request with evidence (pilot metrics).
5) After 2 successful pilot batches (consistent IAA and QA), promote task to production pricing.

Exception handling and retention waivers:
- Retention waivers must be recorded as a short-form ADR in Applied ML with owner signoff and expiration date.
- Emergency retention freeze (e.g., ongoing incident triage): applied-ml-oncall may freeze deletion for up to 30 days; approval and rationale logged.

Audit and compliance:
- Monthly compliance digest emailed to Security & Privacy and Finance summarizing retention transitions, deletions, vendor spend, and active waivers.
- Random third-party audit: once per year, a vendor (approved by Legal) may audit probe handling.

Appendix A — Example probe_catalog SQL snippets:
-- Mark candidates for cold move
UPDATE probe_catalog
SET retention_tier = 'cold', last_moved_to_cold = now()
WHERE retention_tier = 'hot'
  AND created_at < now() - interval '180 days'
  AND last_accessed < now() - interval '90 days'
  AND sensitivity_level != 'restricted';

-- Deletion audit entry
INSERT INTO retention_audit_log (probe_id, action, initiator, ts, note)
VALUES ('p-12345', 'delete', 'data-request-team', now(), 'customer erasure token 9x8x7');
